content: Etravirine reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of lurbinectedin by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of macimorelin by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider an alternative drug. Additionally, coadministration of macimorelin with strong CYP3A4 inducers may lead to false-positive test results. Discontinue the strong CYP3A4 inducer and allow for sufficient washout time before testing. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of macitentan by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inducers should not be coadministered with macitentan. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of midostaurin by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may significantly reduce midostaurin concentrations, leading to decreased efficacy. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of etravirine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of neratinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Netupitant is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4, and its use should be avoided in patients chronically using strong CYP3A4 inducers. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of olaparib by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers cannot be avoided, be aware of the potential for reduced efficacy of olaparib. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of olutasidenib by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers reduce olutasidenib plasma concentrations and efficacy. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid concomitant use of osimertinib with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of palovarotene by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Phenytoin reduces the levels or effects of etravirine by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Etravirine and phenytoin should not be coadministered, as phenytoin increases etravirine metabolism, leading to decreased plasma concentrations and loss of therapeutic effect. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, increase the pirtobrutinib dose as per specific recommendations. Etravirine increases the levels of pomalidomide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter but decreases its levels by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of ponatinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefits outweigh the risks of ponatinib underexposure. Monitor for reduced efficacy. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of pralsetinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, double the pralsetinib dose starting on Day 7 of coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inducer. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inducer for at least 14 days. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of pretomanid by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid is a CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
